name: TubeGen AI
tagline: AI generator for YouTube scripts, titles, descriptions, tags and thumbnail concepts.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a prompt library with a form on top of it. The actual work is sending channel context plus a topic to a language model and rendering structured output: hook, script beats, three title variants, description with timestamps, tag list, thumbnail text ideas. None of that requires anything the vendor owns, and the model doing the lifting is one you can call directly for pennies. An agent can build a local version with saved channel presets, a history table and CSV export in a single sitting. The caveat: if the product also renders finished faceless videos and pushes them to YouTube, that part is a weekend with OAuth and ffmpeg pain, not a one-shot.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you pick a channel preset, type a topic, and get a script outline plus title, description, tag and thumbnail variants saved to a searchable history.
requirements: an LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic) in .env
willingness to write your own prompt templates, which is the actual product
whatYouLose: Prompt templates tuned by someone who watched what performs, so your first outputs will be blander
Any real keyword or search volume data, your tag lists are guesses
One-click publishing or scheduling to YouTube
Thumbnail image generation if the paid tool actually renders images rather than describing them
A polished UI and a mobile-friendly flow for drafting on the phone
moatNotes: The moat is prompt craft and workflow convenience, both of which erode every time a new base model ships.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because fiddling with prompts is the part creators hate, and a tool that hands you ten usable titles in one click is worth a subscription if you upload weekly. Paying also buys the illusion that someone has already figured out what the algorithm likes, which is comforting even when it is mostly vibes. If the product does video assembly and direct upload, the convenience is genuine and the DIY gap is real.
notes: Rename the prompt file to prompts.ts and accept that you now maintain your own prompt library forever.
prompt:
Build a local-only YouTube content generator. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/app.db, created on first run
- Anthropic or OpenAI SDK, key read from .env (API_KEY, MODEL), never hardcoded
- Runs with: npm install && npm run dev

Features in scope:
1. Channel presets table: name, niche, audience, tone, average video length, example titles that performed well. Full CRUD on a /presets page.
2. Generate page: pick a preset, type a topic, choose output types via checkboxes (hook, script outline, full script, titles, description, tags, thumbnail text ideas).
3. One model call per generation. Ask for strict JSON matching a zod schema; validate and retry once on parse failure. Stream nothing, just show a spinner.
4. Results view: titles as a copy-on-click list, script outline as collapsible beats, description with auto-inserted timestamp placeholders, tags as comma-joined text with a copy button.
5. Save every generation to SQLite with preset id, topic, raw JSON, model name, timestamp. /history page with text search and delete.
6. Export a generation to Markdown and all history to CSV.
7. Store prompt templates in src/prompts.ts as plain exported strings so they are easy to edit. Include one solid default template per output type.

Explicitly out of scope: thumbnail image generation, YouTube API upload, keyword volume data, video rendering, multi-user auth, payments.

Deliverables: working app, README with setup and the .env keys, .env.example, and a seed script that inserts one example preset.
